notes: Evaluation protocol is ambiguous: the paper uses the official per-protocol train/test files (Table II, SMOTE on training only, test distribution preserved) but also says five-fold cross-validation is employed (Sec. VI-B; Conclusion says reliability was 'validated through five-fold cross-validation'); which produced Tables IV/VI/VIII is not said, so statistic/n_runs are not_reported and split.protocol is 'official' with k_folds null. Metric tables print fractions under '(in %)' headers; averaging of precision/recall/F1 for the multiclass scenarios is not stated (recall equals accuracy for the TM in Tables VI/VIII, suggesting weighted averaging, not verified). Sec. VI-B mentions 'extracting salient features' but no feature selection is described for Scenarios 1-2 (NN input layers are 27 and 38 = all features); Scenario 3 uses the 11 common features. bits_per_feature/n_boolean_features left not_reported: n_bins=5 one-hot gives at most 5 bits per feature, but quantile bins collapse for low-cardinality features (flags) and the paper gives no total. Whether the KBinsDiscretizer/scaler were fit on training data only is not stated. Sec. VI-A says all algorithms were implemented in Keras on TensorFlow 2.2.0; the TM library is not named (the 'weighted clauses' parameter name suggests tmu or pyTsetlinMachine, not recorded). In Scenario 1 SMOTE is described for the training data generally while Table III also gives class_weight=balanced to DT/RF/LR; whether baselines saw SMOTE data in Scenario 1 is unclear. Scenario 3 sizes (record null) from Fig. 14 if attributed train-first: train 1,674,270, test 759,403. Table IX literature numbers: text p. 2 says [11] DNN 78% / LSTM 79% six-class, table gives 0.78.
